jane_acme: Hey team — after moving our runtime to the Private deployment (VPC) we started getting 401 invalid_api_key on every request. Same code + key works fine against hosted. Any ideas?

sam_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact curl you used (with the key redacted if needed) and the raw response? Also, which header are you sending the key in (Authorization: Bearer vs X-Redwood-Api-Key)?

jane_acme: here's what I ran (sanitized):
```bash
curl -v 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rwd_XXXXX_REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://private.acme.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
response: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": {"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid API key provided"}
}
We set REDWOOD_API_KEY in the container env to the same value. Works against hosted URL but not private.

maya_eng: thanks — couple quick checks: 1) Private deployments require keys to be registered on the Private control plane / tenant (keys from hosted aren't auto-synced). 2) The auth header format you're using (Authorization: Bearer) is supported, but if you've got a sidecar/proxy in front it might rewrite headers. 3) check for stray whitespace/newlines when env var is loaded.

sam_support: Can you run a verbose request and also show the exact request headers the server sees? If you have access to the private agent logs, `journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200` (or the equivalent container stdout) around the time of the request should help — it logs auth failures with a short reason. Don't paste the full key here, just the key fingerprint if available.

jane_acme: grabbed logs from the agent — redacting key chars but copying the lines:
```
Mar 22 14:12:03 redwood-agent[2378]: auth: lookup key 'rwd_XXXXX' for tenant 'acme' -> not found
Mar 22 14:12:03 redwood-agent[2378]: http: auth failure -> invalid_api_key
```
Also checked the container env by exec'ing in: `env | grep REDWOOD` -> shows `REDWOOD_API_KEY=` (empty). We had set the env var in the systemd unit for the app but the deploy script overwrote it during start.

ivan_infra: that's the smoking gun — the agent log says key not found and your container shows an empty env var. Two separate things: a) the Private control plane won't accept keys that aren't registered to that tenant; b) if the process is starting with an empty key, it will obviously send nothing and the agent will reject. For remediation:
- Confirm the key exists in Private: private console -> Settings -> API keys (or the on-prem equivalent). If it's not there, create/import a key in the Private tenant.
- If you want to reuse a hosted key, you'll need to copy it into the Private tenant (we don't sync hosted keys automatically).
- Fix the deploy so REDWOOD_API_KEY is injected into the runtime (check systemd unit, k8s secret mount, or entrypoint wrapper).

sam_support: Quick reproduction steps and commands to gather evidence for our logs:
1) On a dev host where you can reproduce: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-key>" https://private.<your-tenant>/v1/ping` — note the 401/200.
2) On the Private control plane host: `sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -f --since "5 minutes ago"` then re-run the curl to capture the auth line.
3) Check runtime env: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- printenv | grep REDWOOD` or `docker exec -it <container> env | grep REDWOOD`.
4) In the Private console: Settings -> API keys -> look up fingerprint or created_at timestamp.

jane_acme: followed ivan's steps: key was not present in Private (we had only created it in hosted). I imported a new key in Private, updated the k8s secret to the correct value, and restarted the pod.

jane_acme: after restart:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer rwd_YYYY_VALID" https://private.acme.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "id": "g-abc123", "choices": [ { "text": "hi" } ] }
```
Works now.

sam_support: great, thanks for confirming — marking this resolved on our side. We'll add a short KB blurb: "Keys are tenant-scoped in Private; you must import/create keys in your Private control plane. Hosted keys are not auto-imported."

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-3281 attached, escalated to infra for a short audit of your deploy unit file to avoid env overwrite. :white_check_mark:

maya_eng: notes for follow-up: add a small probe during deploy to fail early if REDWOOD_API_KEY is missing, and improve our docs to highlight tenant-scoping difference between Hosted and Private.

jane_acme: thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
